Chinese researchers say the Batan Islands “constitute a natural geographical extension of Taiwan, with sovereignty belonging to China” SeaLight (@SeaLightFound) 🚨BREAKING -- 🇨🇳Chinese scholars have "concluded" that the 🇵🇭#Philippines' northernmost Batanes Islands legally belong to #China, by way of 🇹🇼#Taiwan. At a June 30th symposium in Guangzhou hosted by Jinan University, roughly a dozen researchers from prominent Chinese universities and institutes declared that Manila's control over Batanes lacks historical and legal basis, and in fact the islands belong to China. "Participants unanimously concluded that the Batan Islands constitute a natural geographical extension of Taiwan, with sovereignty belonging to China, and that so-called Japan-Philippines maritime delimitation negotiations in the area hold no legal validity. The symposium was convened in direct response to the joint statement issued at the recent Japan-Philippines summit." [Link in the comments below] In other words, Beijing -- via its academics and aided by state media -- clearly orchestrated this symposium to propose a new territorial baseline, a "lawfare" tactic to back up the patrols it launched far to the east of Taiwan last month. So far PRC government officials have not endorsed the symposium's conclusions, but that's not unusual in PRC gray-zone narrative warfare. For now, muddying the waters over Batanes' legal ownership is sufficient to help justify its "sovereignty" patrols. Full SeaLight analysis coming soon. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/SeaLightFound/status/2075010896863396350#m

India-Australia meetings are much like cricket: The agenda is as focused as a One-Day International. The decisions are as fast as T20 cricket. The partnership is as long-lasting and deep as a Test match.

Today’s talks have unparalleled outcomes in areas such as renewable energy, climate action, nuclear energy, critical minerals, technology, education and more. Another highlight is the issuing of an important declaration to strengthen defence and security cooperation. Equally noteworthy is our discussions to work closely in shipbuilding, ship repair and maintenance.

Held wide-ranging discussions with Prime Minister Albanese in Melbourne this afternoon. The India-Australia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership of 2022 has continuously expanded the scope of our cooperation. We have now decided to accelerate work on the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation, with unprecedented progress over the past few years. We talked about how to add more vigour to trade and investment linkages. The Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) will be balanced, ambitious and beneficial for both countries. @AlboMP

Наші воїни виконують план далекобійних санкцій у відповідь на затягування війни і російські удари. Напередодні були важливі ураження по обʼєктах, які забезпечують російський нафтовий комплекс та працюють на воєнну політику. Воїни СБУ уразили дві нафтобази – у Ставрополі та Твері. Обидві приблизно за 500 кілометрів від лінії фронту. Також підрозділи Сил оборони України уразили резервне сховище для накопичення та зберігання пального. Відстань від лінії фронту – близько 800 кілометрів. В російській Уфі застосували санкції по нафтоперекачувальній станції майже за 1500 кілометрів від нашого кордону. А також був санкціонований нафтоналивний термінал у Ростовському регіоні, що приблизно за 200 кілометрів від лінії фронту. Дякую всім нашим воїнам, які щодня роблять такі результати можливими. Ми давно запропонували Росії закінчити цю війну, і кожен день затягування має приносити відчуття війни туди, звідки це все й почалося, – в Росію.

Our warriors are carrying out the long-range sanctions plan in response to Russia dragging out the war and continuing its attacks. Recent days saw important successful strikes on facilities supporting Russia's oil sector and sustaining its war policy. SSU warriors struck two oil depots – one in Stavropol and the other in Tver. Both are about 500 kilometers from the front line. Units of Ukraine's Defense Forces also struck a reserve fuel storage facility located about 800 kilometers from the front. An oil pumping station in Russia's Ufa, nearly 1,500 kilometers from our border, also came under sanctions. An oil loading terminal in the Rostov region, about 200 kilometers from the front line, was sanctioned as well. I thank all our warriors who make results like these possible every single day. We offered Russia a way to end this war long ago, and every day it chooses to prolong it should bring the reality of war back to where it began – to Russia. Video

With its strikes on Moscow, Ukraine is taking disruption to a new level. The success of a long-range strike is not measured by impact alone. Even an intercepted attack closes airspace, disrupts flights and logistics, and erodes the sense of security. Russia cannot protect everything. It has more targets than air defences. Hitting the target magnifies the effect, but disruption begins before destruction. Yes, Russia will continue firing ballistic missiles at Ukrainian cities. But Putin’s problem is that Ukrainian suffering will no longer compensate Russians for disruption at home. As that disruption spreads, Russians will increasingly blame Putin and his corrupt regime for breaking the central bargain underpinning his rule since 2022: war was supposed to be something Ukrainians suffer, not them. The choice is Putin’s: wind down the war to preserve control, or tighten control at home to keep the war going. I would love to be wrong, but everything we know about him suggests he will choose the latter.

Islamabad: 9 July 2026. H.E. Dr. Gordan Grlić Radman, Minister for Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Croatia, called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House in Islamabad, today. Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister Sen. Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Foreign Secretary Amb. Amna Baloch were also present. During the warm and cordial meeting, the Prime Minister welcomed the Croatian Foreign Minister and his delegation to Pakistan. He stated that Pakistan enjoyed friendly relations with Croatia, marked by cordiality, mutual respect and shared interest. He expressed Pakistan’s desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly through enhanced trade and investment, information technology, connectivity, agriculture, tourism and skilled manpower. While conveying his warm regards and good wishes to President Zoran Milanovic and Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic, the Prime Minister extended a cordial invitation to both leaders to undertake official visits to Pakistan, at their kind convenience. The Croatian Foreign Minister thanked the Prime Minister for the warm welcome and said that he was honored to visit Islamabad and congratulated Pakistan and its leadership, on playing a prominent role in regional peace efforts. He also expressed his Government’s desire to enhance Pakistan-Croatia ties in all areas of mutual interest. Video
Minister for Foreign and European Affairs of the Republic of Croatia, H.E Dr. Gordan Grlić Radman calls on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif. Islamabad, 9 July 2026.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 received H.E. Both sides discussed ways to strengthen ties in the field of trade, investment, agriculture, labour mobility, visa facilitation, education, defence, climate change, tourism, infrastructure, and IT. They also exchanged views on various facets of Pakistan-EU cooperation as well as regional and global issues of interest. Recognizing that connectivity lies at the heart of sustainable development, regional stability, and global economic integration, the two sides discussed the possibilities and potential for collaboration between the ports of Pakistan and Croatia. Both sides agreed to hold Bilateral Political Consultations during the current year or early 2027. The visit marks an important step in strengthening relations between the two countries.

ICRIER convened an Expert Consultation on "Streamlining the Indian Spices Market: Issues and Way Forward" on 8 July 2026, bringing together policymakers, scientists, nutritionists, and industry leaders to deliberate on how food safety standards can be uniformly implemented across India's spices supply chain. Key takeaways: 🔸 India accounts for over 40% of global spice production and produces around 75 spice varieties, yet FSSAI has vertical standards for only 45, and Codex Alimentarius for just 14. 🔸 Spices are India's third-largest agricultural export, but 60-80% of the domestic market remains informal, with wide variation in quality and no standard database on domestic food safety rejections. 🔸 Lack of uniformity in testing procedures across spice testing laboratories of multiple agencies is adding an estimated INR 25,000-30,000 in compliance costs per sample. 🔸 Panelists agreed that most regulatory gaps stem from inconsistent enforcement and a lack of reliable data, not the design of standards themselves. 🔸 Recommendations include a single nodal agency to regulate the spice supply chain from farm to retail, and FSSAI leading international standard-setting as host secretariat for the Codex Committee on Spices and Culinary Herbs. The event marked the release of ICRIER's report "Streamlining the Indian Spices Market: Issues and Way Forward" by Dr Ramesh Chand, Distinguished Professor, ICRIER and Former Member, NITI Aayog, and Dr Raka Saxena, Programme Director – Agriculture Policy, NITI Aayog. 📄 Full report: icrier.org/publications/stre… #ICRIER #SpicesPolicy #FoodSafety #FSSAI #AgriPolicy #India

H. E. Dr Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of Foreign Trade of the United Arab Emirates and the accompanying delegation paid a courtesy call on Minister for Foreign Affairs Hon. Mr Shisir Khanal, at the Ministry today. During the meeting, the two Ministers exchanged views on strengthening bilateral relations between Nepal and the United Arab Emirates across a range of areas of mutual interest, including greater cooperation in trade, investment, AI, digital transformation, tourism, labour migration, infrastructure, renewable energy as well as increased Sovereign Wealth Fund investment in priority sectors. Hon. Foreign Minister further underscored the enduring friendship and growing cooperation between the two countries while highlighting the Government of Nepal's aspiration to make the upcoming Golden Jubilee celebration of diplomatic relations a major milestone by securing UAE investment in various projects in Nepal. The Hon. Minister also urged the UAE Government to remove the requirement of further verification of the Police Report after attestation by the Department of Consular Services.

A must-read article from @abcnews highlights some of the major issues with any potential return to war for the United States. Not only is the blockade built on a fundamentally flawed premise that economic constriction would bring Iran to its knees in an existential war, but the blockade failed to meaningfully impact the single biggest factor in the “$500M/day” in losses that Washington claimed: Oil. Before the war, Iran was selling its sanctioned oil at a discount for about $53 a barrel, according to Obsidian Risk Advisors sanctions specialist Brett Erickson. But the war created scarcity conditions and the price of oil shot up. "In May, yes, we have a blockade imposed, but Iran still had so much oil outside the blockade line that they were able to sell it at $117 per barrel," Mr Erickson said. "So the price of the oil had more than doubled and Iran was able to really over achieve their revenues throughout the first half of the year by about 30 per cent beyond what they had projected." The Iranian budgetary year begins in March but using that rate of sale for a calendar year, Mr Erickson said Tehran "projected that they would make about $35.5 billion this year in their oil revenues". "In a six-month time period from January to July 1, you're looking at $17.75 billion," he said. Analysing available Iranian oil sales data and Chinese imports information, Mr Erickson estimates Tehran generated more than $23 billion from oil sales in the first half of 2026, exceeding its own pre-war forecasts. Mr Erickson said Iran was able to move about 55 million barrels out of the region in the first 14 days of the MOU being in place, wiping out the impact of the blockade in the first half of June. "By flooding those tankers out to the market, getting them outside of any potential reimposed US blockade line, moving empty tankers in that can draw down those onshore storage … [Iran could] essentially get a complete reset of their oil storage," he said. "Which makes it untenable to posit that one could reimpose a blockade and cause these oil well shut-ins, which were a very flawed premise in the first place, but it essentially wipes that off the board entirely." abc.net.au/news/2026-07-09/i…

The Archaeological Survey of India is honoured to undertake the conservation of Prambanan Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia, under the India–Indonesia Collaborative Conservation initiative jointly launched by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and President of Indonesia, Prabowo Subianto. This landmark collaboration is a testament to the enduring civilisational ties between India and Indonesia, reflecting a shared commitment to preserving our rich cultural heritage and passing it on to future generations. Dating back to the 10th century CE, Prambanan Temple is Indonesia's largest Hindu temple complex dedicated to Shiva. The sprawling complex consists of 240 temples, with three magnificent central shrines devoted to Shiva, Vishnu, and Brahma. These are accompanied by three temples dedicated to their respective vahanas (divine mounts), while beautifully carved reliefs narrating the story of the Ramayana adorn the temple walls.

خشونت علیه هزاره‌های کویته از اواخر دهه‌ی ۱۹۹۰ وارد مرحله‌ای تازه شد. اگر تا پیش از آن، تبلیغات فرقه‌ای و تهدیدهای پراکنده علیه شیعیان وجود داشت، از سال ۱۹۹۹ الگوی حملات به ترورهای هدفمند و سپس به کشتارهای جمعی تغییر یافت. پژوهشگران این روند را به سه مرحله تقسیم می‌کنند: نخست، تبلیغات و نفرت‌پراکنی فرقه‌ای؛ دوم، ترور شخصیت‌های برجسته‌ی هزاره؛ و سوم، حملات گسترده با هدف کشتار جمعی غیرنظامیان. نقطه عطف این دوره، ترور سردار نثارعلی هزاره، وزیر آموزش ایالت بلوچستان، در ۵ اکتبر ۱۹۹۹ بود. افراد مسلح او را هنگام خروج از ساختمان دبیرخانه ایالت در کویته هدف قرار دادند. راننده و محافظ او کشته شدند و خود او نیز به‌شدت زخمی شد. این حمله آغاز موجی از ترورهای هدفمند علیه جامعه‌ی هزاره بود. در فاصله سال‌های ۱۹۹۹ تا ۲۰۰۳ دست‌کم ۱۷ نفر از شخصیت‌های برجسته‌ی هزاره، از جمله داکتران، انجنیران، وکلا، بازرگانان، کارمندان دولت و دانشجویان، در حملات مسلحانه کشته شدند. در بیشتر این پرونده‌ها، عاملان هرگز محاکمه نشدند. سال ۲۰۰۳ نقطه تغییر در الگوی خشونت بود. در ۸ جون، افراد مسلح موتر حامل دانشجویان پولیس هزاره را در مسیر آکادمی پولیس هدف قرار دادند. در این حمله ۱۲ پولیس کشته و نُه نفر زخمی شدند. کم‌تر از یک ماه بعد، در ۴ جولای، سه مهاجم مسلح وارد امام‌باره‌ای در سرک میچنگی (Mechangi Road) شدند و نمازگزاران را به گلوله بستند. در این حمله دست‌کم ۴۷ تا ۵۳ نفر کشته و ده‌ها نفر دیگر زخمی شدند. گروه لشکر جهنگوی مسئولیت این حمله را بر عهده گرفت. این رویداد، نخستین کشتار جمعی گسترده‌ی هزاره‌ها در کویته به شمار می‌رود. در ۲۴ مارچ ۲۰۰۴، هم‌زمان با مراسم عاشورا در نزدیکی لیاقت‌بازار کویته، افراد مسلح از چند نقطه به دسته‌ی عزاداران تیراندازی کردند و نارنجک پرتاب کردند. دست‌کم ۳۶ نفر کشته و ده‌ها نفر زخمی شدند. این حمله نشان داد که عاملان دیگر تنها افراد مشخص را هدف قرار نمی‌دهند، بلکه تجمع‌های مذهبی و غیرنظامیان نیز به اهداف اصلی آنان تبدیل شده‌اند. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/256966

According to their legal team, the judge cited the family's failure to include lessons on gender, sex education, "tolerance and diversity," and even pointed to the girls' preference for religious and classical music over popular genres. The parents say they began homeschooling during the COVID-19 pandemic after losing confidence in their daughters' schools. They remain free while appealing what their attorneys believe is the first criminal prosecution of its kind in Brazil.

There seems to be a conception that if US air defense systems are exhausted then the US has to capitulate. This is fundamentally incorrect. The only way to get any adversary to capitulate is to destroy their will to fight. Air defense systems are actually a de-escalation measure, because they limit damage to allies that would otherwise become a call for escalation. In any escalating scenario, the US has an unmatched advantage. The US can essentially instantly delete any target it wants with zero risk to its own personnel in about 20 different ways, from individual vehicles up to entire cities. The US's adversaries should pray that the US never runs out of air defense, so they can keep lobbing their puny and obviously ineffective missiles at their neighbors in a spate of infantile rage, because if they were to land enough hits, the US would switch from nation building to nation destroying. This last occurred in 1941 and was a rough time for all involved. The only difference is that now the US is far richer and far more advanced relative to the tiny club of insane despots who treat their own subjects (citizens would be too strong a word for people who have no civic rights) with even more contempt than they do the US, whose wealth and power drives them mad with envy. It has become extremely clear that 99.9% of the world is thrilled to run some form of peaceful free trade capitalism and get super rich within the more-than-effective deterrence envelope of 2026 norms around rules of engagement. The 0.1% evidently cannot be deterred by sub-meter precision blowing up their stuff or the surgical deletion of their political colleagues, so one might sensibly ask: What will destroy their will to fight or their ability to continue to wreck it all for everyone else? Polish FlyEye is a decent drone. But it has a couple of problems: - price: $200 000 per drone (as far as I remember) is way to expensive in a modern warfare. Russian army builds an eco system that will consist of EW, small radar stations, FPV IN drones. The survival of a drone like that might be very low in a modern conditions; - bad thermal camera; - acts quite good against Russian EW; - quite sensitive in terms of weather conditions (wind); - quite good and comfortable for a pilot Here in Ukraine we have an ISR drones that have Israel’s thermal cameras which are really good. Fly the same amount of time in the air. Have much better resistance against the wind. With the price of $15-17 000. It’s not just about a Polish drone. It’s about all the Western drones in general I would say. The price is too high. If you prepare your army to fight a war (not just fly a drone for years during a peace time) you need to understand that. P.S. in 2023 my company and I tested their Warmate also. It was…Well, you don’t see them being used in Ukraine right now. The U.S. Department of Energy instructed AI data centers to stop using electricity from the main power grid. As temperatures exceeded 100 degrees Fahrenheit across much of the eastern United States Energy Secretary Chris Wright ordered data centers and other major electricity consumers on the PJM grid to switch to backup generators. The purpose was to conserve power so that homes could continue running air conditioners during one of the hottest periods of the year. The PJM grid serves 13 states and includes northern Virginia which hosts the largest cluster of data centers in the world. These centers support AI systems cloud computing streaming services and much of the internet but they require massive amounts of electricity. Officials explained that backup generators would ease strain on the grid and help avoid blackouts while millions of air conditioners operated at peak levels. This action illustrates how the rapid growth of AI infrastructure is starting to compete with regular household electricity needs during extreme heat waves. There are drawbacks to the solution. Most backup generators burn diesel or natural gas which creates more local air pollution than power from large plants. The region also has limited battery storage compared to states like California and Texas making it challenging to handle demand surges with cleaner sources. As AI data centers expand across the country experts predict that extreme heat events will increasingly challenge the ability of the power grid to meet both technological and everyday needs.

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, addressed the National Workshop on Strengthening Tribal Research Institutes, organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in Bhubaneswar. The workshop focused on strengthening research, technology, governance, institutional capacity and partnerships to build Tribal Research Institutes into stronger knowledge and policy institutions. Dr. Balasubramaniam called for Tribal Research Institutes to broaden their research agenda to better understand the social, political, economic and cultural transitions shaping tribal communities. He emphasised that research must move beyond data to listening by respecting tribal belief systems, lived experiences and traditional wisdom, and that TRIs should serve as anthropological knowledge repositories, policy think tanks and advocates for tribal voices, while humanising data through ground truthing and community perspectives. Recognising indigenous knowledge as a national resource, he called for its documentation, preservation and recognition, and methodologies to account for its contribution to India’s Gross Domestic Knowledge Product. As AI reshapes the future, preserving indigenous knowledge and strengthening tribal-led research become even more critical. The workshop also launched TribeX, a digital learning platform for tribal arts, culture, languages, traditional knowledge and skill development. #TribalDevelopment #IndigenousKnowledge @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp @drrbalu

Never-before-seen footage of the private island of convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein gives a detailed tour of the hideaway to which a number of survivors allege they were trafficked and exploited. Ion Nicola, a Romanian artist who told Storyful he worked for Epstein from 2010 to 2019 – carrying out work in a number of buildings – filmed this footage as he drove around the island of Little Saint James. The video starts with a view of one of the island’s bays as Nicola drives along a single-track road in a golf cart. His drive reveals a huge sun dial, and a gorilla statue – one of a number of large stone statues on the island. The footage shows manicured lawns, plants, and various paths; a view of a pier and beach shows several boats present. A number of shaded areas are seen along the beach, with two further human-like statues marking one of them. Nicola then drives up a hill and, as the camera turns, a pool house is seen by the cliff edge. Nicola gets out of the vehicle at the main residence on the island, which has a large pool area. As he walks to the terrace of the building, a large “E” is seen below. Nicola told Storyful he was the artist responsible for the interior artwork in the island’s mosque-like Five Palms building. He included footage of the building, which is blue- and white-striped, with a mosaic-style red and white patio surrounding it. In an interview with the New York Times from April, Nicola confirmed that Epstein regularly called the building his “mosque”. Among other tasks, Epstein asked for a design replacing the Arabic word for God with his initials in English, Nicola said. “Remember we saw the Arabic writing in black and white,” he wrote to Nicola in an email, “instead of allah, i thought j’s and e ‘s” (sic). According to the Romanian journalist Mircea Barbu, Nicola’s name appears 2,578 times in the so-called Epstein Files of correspondence. Nicola, however, has not been accused of any wrongdoing. The Five Palms featured in images released by the US Oversight Committee in December 2025, with a wide shot of the building and interior, which appears empty, save for a solitary bed frame and mattress. Epstein died while awaiting trial in 2019. A New York City medical examiner ruled his death a suicide. In 2022, the attorney general of the US Virgin Islands announced a civil settlement of more than $105 million with Epstein’s estate and other co-defendants, relating to an action filed in 2020 under anti-criminal enterprise, sex trafficking, child exploitation and fraud laws of the Virgin Islands. In 2023, Little Saint James was purchased, along with another Epstein-owned island, Great Saint James, for $60 million by Florida billionaire Stephen Deckoff, who announced plans to develop a luxury private resort. Alexandra de Hoop Scheffer (@AdeHoopScheffer) The transition from a US- to a Europe-led security order is no longer theoretical. It is underway. The Trump administration's announced reduction in American military capabilities in Europe and the undertaking of a broader force review marks the first step in a structural burden-shift that no successor is likely to reverse. Whether that shift opens a window of opportunity or of vulnerability depends on the speed and sustainability of Europe’s response, and on Washington’s view of a stronger European industrial base as an asset instead of a competitive threat. European NATO members and Canada raised defense spending by 20% in real terms in 2025, bringing their combined total to $574 billion. Yet the central paradox is stark: Europe is beginning to spend for wartime while still procuring and planning for peacetime. Closing that gap is the defining defense policy challenge of this decade, and it requires three urgent measures. 1️⃣ First, align procurement with threat reality and use Ukrainian expertise. The ReArm Europe plan is a start, but ambition must be matched by ruthless industrial pragmatism. Europe faces a real dilemma: rebuilding its defense-industrial base for long-term autonomy while urgently closing immediate capability gaps. These goals are not mutually exclusive, but they require balancing. Ukraine, now a co-architect of European security, is central to this, as European defense firms move from supplying Kyiv to co-developing combat-proven technology. 2️⃣ Second, include the private sector. Defense and security policy in Europe has long been the preserve of governments and militaries. That model is obsolete in an era when the most consequential capabilities—autonomous systems, AI-enabled intelligence, cybersecurity, and satellite communications—are being built in commercial labs. Policymakers must treat technology companies not as contractors but as strategic partners that must be in discussions to set industrial priorities. 3️⃣ Third, reframe the transatlantic bargain as strategic complementarity. Washington must encourage Europe to build its own industrial base, not treat it as a competitive threat. Strategic complementarity—not dependency—is the model that works for both sides. Complementarity is particularly apparent in defense tech. The U.S. leads in AI-enabled systems, space-based intelligence, and autonomous platforms; Europe's strengths lie in advanced manufacturing, sovereign cyber capabilities, laser technology, and a rapidly maturing dual-use deep tech ecosystem. 🚨 The NATO summit in Ankara should be the moment allies stop relitigating the terms of the alliance and formalize a new framework of strategic complementarity through agreed capability targets, a transatlantic defense innovation compact, and a shared framework for managing the transition without breaking the alliance. За останні 3 роки та 8 місяців (44 місяці або 1350 днів) ворог захопив 23% Донецької області, а під контролем Сил Оборони України залишається 22.6% Хоч динаміка окупації Донеччини залишається у розрізі щоденних оновлень доволі жвавою, але в контексті контролю над усієї областю — дуже повільною. До повномасштабного вторгнення бойовики терористичних проросійських угруповань контролювали приблизно 32% області. National water availability data at your fingertips! 💧🎉 The National Water Availability Assessment Data Companion provides regularly updated, model-based estimates of water availability and use on a national scale. Nearly 27 million Americans, or 8% of the U.S. population, live in areas where water demand consistently approaches or exceeds naturally available water supply. Until recently, accessing comprehensive water availability information with national coverage required stitching together disparate datasets across multiple agencies, regions, and complicated websites. The Data Companion eliminates these barriers by: 💧 Providing consistent information about water availability and use across approximately 80,000 watersheds nationwide from 2000 to 2020 💧 Enabling data access through various user-friendly means, including a subset and download tool, a data file directory, an API, and a new interactive map 💧 Continually adding new and updated data to reflect the latest USGS water models and science Check out the interactive map now: water.usgs.gov/nwaa-data/ 📷 1: View of soil moisture data for January 2020 across the lower 48 United States from the Data Companion web mapper.

An outreach programme on the Income Tax Act, 2025, Income Tax Rules, 2026, and TDS-related issues was organised today at DRDO Bhawan by the Directorate of Management & Security (DMS), DRDO. The programme commenced with an address by Dr. Ravindra Singh, DG (R&M), who highlighted the importance of awareness and compliance with the latest income tax provisions. The technical sessions were delivered by Ms. Beenu, Additional Commissioner of Income Tax; Shri Y. N. Saxena, Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax; and the team from Aaykar Bhawan, New Delhi who provided detailed insights into the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025, Income Tax Rules, 2026, and TDS-related issues while addressing participants' queries. The interactive sessions enhanced participants understanding of the new tax framework and strengthened statutory compliance among DDOs and PAOs across DRDO. The programme concluded with a Vote of Thanks by the Director DMS.

महाराष्ट्र-कर्नाटक सीमाप्रश्न सोडविण्यासाठी सर्वतोपरी लढा सुरूच राहणार मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली आज विधान भवन, मुंबई येथे महाराष्ट्र-कर्नाटक सीमा प्रश्नाबाबत उच्चाधिकार समितीची बैठक पार पडली. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस म्हणाले, महाराष्ट्र-कर्नाटक सीमाप्रश्नी महाराष्ट्र सरकार सीमाभागातील मराठी बांधवांच्या पाठीशी ठामपणे उभे असून, त्यांच्या न्याय्य हक्कांसाठी सर्वतोपरी प्रयत्न सुरूच राहतील. सीमाभागातील मराठी बांधवांच्या न्याय्य हक्कांचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी सरकार सर्वतोपरी प्रयत्न करेल. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, महाराष्ट्र-कर्नाटक सीमाप्रश्नासंदर्भात अनेक वर्षांपासून सातत्याने संघर्ष सुरू आहे. मा. सर्वोच्च न्यायालयातील सीमाप्रश्नाची सुनावणी लवकर सुरू व्हावी, यासाठी वरिष्ठ कायदेतज्ज्ञ नियुक्त करण्यात येणार असून, कर्नाटकमध्ये मराठी बांधवांवर दाखल करण्यात आलेल्या विविध खटल्यांच्या संदर्भात त्यांना सक्षम कायदेशीर मदत उपलब्ध करून देणार आहोत. सीमाभागातील मराठी बांधवांना विविध अडचणींचा सामना करावा लागत असून, संपूर्ण महाराष्ट्र त्यांच्या पाठीशी ठामपणे उभा आहे. समितीने मांडलेल्या सर्व सूचना आणि प्रलंबित मुद्द्यांवर सरकार आवश्यक ती कार्यवाही करण्यास तयार आहे. भाषिक अल्पसंख्याकांच्या आयोगाबाबतची सर्व माहिती संकलित करून महाराष्ट्रातील सर्व खासदारांना पाठविण्यात येईल, जेणेकरून हा विषय संसदेत प्रभावीपणे मांडता येईल. सर्वोच्च न्यायालयातील सीमाप्रश्नाची सुनावणी लवकर सुरू व्हावी, यासाठी राज्य सरकारच्या वतीने आवश्यक अर्ज दाखल करण्यात येतील. तसेच या प्रकरणासाठी आवश्यकतेनुसार वरिष्ठ विधिज्ञांची नियुक्ती करण्याबाबतही कार्यवाही करण्यात येईल. सरकारचे वरिष्ठ कायदेतज्ज्ञही या प्रकरणात सक्रिय भूमिका बजावतील. या खटल्यांसाठी लागणारा खर्च महाराष्ट्र सरकार उचलेल. या Africa’s future will be shaped in its rural economies and areas. Today at @IFAD, I was pleased to co-host with Italy the event “Advancing the Italian Mattei Plan: Scaling Joint Investments in Agriculture and Food Systems.” The #MatteiPlan reflects an important shift in international cooperation with Africa: moving from traditional donor-recipient models towards equal-to-equal partnership, shared ownership, co-investment and mutual benefit. The third annual progress report to the Italian Parliament shows how this approach is moving from vision to implementation across priority areas including agriculture, water, energy, infrastructure, education and health, with IFAD recognized among the international partners supporting this agenda. This direction is closely aligned with IFAD’s mandate. We invest with governments and rural communities to strengthen smallholder agriculture, build resilient value chains, expand access to finance and markets, and create opportunities where they are needed most. Italy and IFAD’s collaboration under the Mattei Plan is now moving from alignment to implementation: Côte d’Ivoire is partnering with Italy and IFAD to advance a major milestone through the Agro-Industrial Pole Project in the North-East. Italy’s €100 million co-financing will complement IFAD’s US$75 million investment to support climate-adaptive agriculture, strengthen value chains and improve food and nutrition security for more than 35,000 rural families, around 220,000 people. The Government of Senegal is working with Italy, IFAD, @TheOPECFund and @EIB on a US$265 million co-investment programme to support food sovereignty and reach more than one million people. With Angola, we are exploring further collaboration in the coffee value chain, drawing on Italian expertise and private sector engagement. These examples show how public investment, technical expertise and private sector partnerships can come together to deliver lasting impact at the first mile of food systems. With more than 60 per cent of IFAD’s portfolio in Africa, and with our country presence, IFAD is a strong partner of the Mattei Plan. As we look towards #IFAD14, with its focus on market integration, employment and resilience, this partnership offers a strong operational platform to scale joint investments with African countries. My thanks to the Government of Italy, Ambassadors from our African Member States, institutional partners and private sector actors for today’s important discussion and for their shared commitment to investing in rural prosperity. @ItalyMFA_int | @GruppoCDP | @Palazzo_Chigi | @SocialMasaf | @MEF_GOV

Statement from Trinamool Congress All funds held in the party’s bank accounts have been fully and transparently disclosed. The party has duly reported all donation transactions to the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Income Tax Department. These disclosures are published annually on the ECI’s website and are available in the public domain. The details relating to electoral bonds are already available with the Government of India, as the bonds were issued by the State Bank of India (SBI) and subsequently submitted to the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India. The Enforcement Directorate’s decision to freeze the party’s bank accounts is a politically motivated act. We strongly condemn this arbitrary and illegal action. The misuse of investigative agencies to target political opponents has become a hallmark of the BJP’s politics and represents a serious assault on democratic institutions and the principles of a level playing field.

پیکر شاپور زدران، ستاره‌ی پیشین تیم ملی کریکت افغانستان، پس از چاشت ام‌روز (چهارشنبه، ۱۷ سرطان) از هند به کابل منتقل شد. شاپور زدران، یکی از چهره‌های برجسته و تأثیرگذار کریکت افغانستان، شام سه‌شنبه پس از چندین ماه مبارزه با بیماری، در یکی از شفاخانه‌های شهر دهلی‌نو هند چشم از جهان فرو بست. او از ماه جنوری سال روان برای درمان بیماری نادر سیستم ایمنی بدن (HLH) در هند بستری بود، اما تلاش پزشکان برای نجات جانش نتیجه نداد. منبع‌های نزدیک به خانواده‌ی زدران گفته‌اند که پیکر این ورزش‌کار پیشین پس از کابل، برای برگزاری مراسم تشییع و خاک‌سپاری به زادگاهش منتقل می‌شود. انتظار می‌رود در این مراسم، عضوهای خانواده، شماری از مقام‌های حکومتی، مسئولان کریکت، ورزش‌کاران و صدها تن از هواداران او حضور داشته باشند. شاپور زدران از پیش‌گامان کریکت افغانستان به شمار می‌رفت و نقش برجسته‌ای در رشد و جهانی‌شدن این رشته ورزشی در کشور داشت. او بین سال‌های ۲۰۰۹ تا ۲۰۲۰ در ۴۴ مسابقه یک‌روزه و ۳۶ دیدار بیست‌آوره برای تیم ملی افغانستان به میدان رفت و با عمل‌کرد درخشان خود، در صعود تیم ملی به رقابت‌های معتبر جهانی، از جمله جام جهانی کریکت، سهم مهمی ایفا کرد. درگذشت شاپور زدران با موج گسترده‌ای از پیام‌های تسلیت از سوی بازی‌کنان، مسئولان کریکت افغانستان و هواداران این ورزش همراه شده‌است. بسیاری از آنان از او به‌عنوان یکی از معماران نسل طلایی کریکت افغانستان یاد کرده و خدماتش به ورزش کشور را ماندگار توصیف کرده‌اند. #خبریک Video

We discussed in detail the energy track and preparations for winter. Everyone is interested in ending this war before winter, but regardless of how events unfold, we must be ready to protect our people and ensure Ukraine’s resilience. I am grateful for the energy support and for the fact that all previous agreements are being implemented. There are new ideas as well. We are working together on the energy security of all of Europe. The Ministry of Home Affairs' Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has issued a public advisory warning against a sharp rise in online matrimonial frauds, where cybercriminals exploit matrimonial websites and apps by posing as wealthy professionals, NRIs, doctors, engineers or Army officers to gain victims' trust. According to the advisory, fraudsters typically build an emotional relationship over days or weeks before seeking money on various pretexts, including customs charges for expensive gifts, travel expenses, visa fees or medical emergencies. Once the payment is made, they either disappear or continue demanding additional funds using new excuses. The government has urged users to remain vigilant and verify every prospective match through video calls, family members, employment details and reverse image searches before placing their trust in someone online. People have also been advised never to transfer money to anyone known only through the internet. Victims or those who suspect cyber fraud should immediately report the incident by calling the national cybercrime helpline 1930 or filing a complaint through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, while preserving chat records, profile links, transaction receipts and other digital evidence to assist investigators. #CyberCrime #MatrimonialFraud #CyberSecurity #DigitalSafety #ScamAlert #MarriageScam #FakeProfiles #MinistryOfHomeAffairs #CyberAwareness#IndiaToday

Crisil के मुताबिक, फरवरी और मार्च में अत्यधिक गर्मी के कारण गर्मियों की फसल की बुवाई में देरी और उत्पादन कम रहने से टमाटर महंगा हुआ. वहीं, प्याज की कीमतों में सालाना आधार पर 2 फीसदी की बढ़ोतरी दर्ज की गई. इसकी वजह अधिक कीमत वाले रबी सीजन के स्टॉक का बाजार में आना रही. रिपोर्ट में कहा गया है कि खाद्य तेल और एलपीजी सिलेंडर की कीमतों में भी सालाना आधार पर 10-10 फीसदी की बढ़ोतरी हुई. इसके पीछे पश्चिम एशिया में जारी संघर्ष के कारण सप्लाई प्रभावित होना एक प्रमुख कारण बताया गया है. हालांकि, ताजा रबी फसल की आवक बढ़ने से आलू की कीमतों में 14 फीसदी की गिरावट दर्ज की गई. इससे थाली की लागत में होने वाली बढ़ोतरी को कुछ हद तक संतुलित करने में मदद मिली. महीने-दर-महीने आधार पर जून में टमाटर की कीमतों में 17 फीसदी, आलू में 5 फीसदी और प्याज में 8 फीसदी की बढ़ोतरी हुई. इसके चलते अन्य खाद्य वस्तुओं में कुछ नरमी के बावजूद शाकाहारी थाली की लागत बढ़ गई. मांसाहारी थाली के महंगा होने की एक और बड़ी वजह ब्रॉयलर चिकन की कीमतों में बढ़ोतरी रही. रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, ब्रॉयलर की कीमतों में सालाना आधार पर अनुमानित 7 फीसदी की ग्रोथ हुई है. चूंकि मांसाहारी थाली की कुल लागत में ब्रॉयलर की हिस्सेदारी करीब 50 फीसदी होती है. इसलिए इसका सीधा असर थाली की कीमत पर पड़ा. Each year, millions of young people enter labour markets across low- and middle-income countries. Yet too many rural economies are not creating enough productive opportunities to absorb them. When opportunities are limited, the effects can be far-reaching. Economic exclusion can fuel instability and increase migratory pressures, with consequences that extend beyond the communities directly affected. Evidence shows that when rural economies grow, so do people’s opportunities to build viable futures at home. Increasing investment in rural development by the equivalent of 1% of GDP can reduce out-migration by nearly one percentage point. Expanding rural employment opportunities is central to this effort. In #Cameroon, the IFAD-funded AEP-Youth programme took an innovative approach to boosting youth employment: tailored business incubators. From poultry farming to snail slime production, more than 30,000 young people benefitted from the start-up kits these incubators provided, including interest-free loans, productive grants and tailored financial products. The programme produced strong results: participants achieved 45.4% higher total gross income and 36.3% higher gross income per capita compared with non-participating households. Additionally, livestock gross income increased by 152.3% while the likelihood of selling products rose by 108.6%. But the programme generated impact far beyond young entrepreneurs themselves – supported enterprises were significantly more likely to hire labour and spent more on wages, pointing to a broader employment creation effect and showing that targeted investments can stimulate local labour demand, strengthening rural economies more broadly. With the right financing instruments, targeted support and evidence-based programme design, rural development can generate jobs, reduce pressures to migrate and contribute to more stable and inclusive growth. WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean Hanan Balkhy says she held key discussions with Afghan officials in Kabul and Kandahar during the Polio Oversight Board mission to Afghanistan on efforts to eradicate polio and expand health services. In a post on X, Balkhy said the meetings emphasized the need to vaccinate every child against wild poliovirus, strengthen disease surveillance, and reinforce routine immunization. She added that strengthening Afghanistan's health system and expanding access to essential healthcare, particularly in remote areas, require sustained international donor support. #TOLOnews_English

The newly appointed Deputy Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Afghanistan, Bruno Lemarquis, has met with Herat Governor Mawlana Islam Jar during his visit to the province to discuss UN programs, economic cooperation, counter-narcotics efforts, and the situation of returning migrants. According to the Herat governor's office, Lemarquis praised the progress made in Herat in combating narcotics, promoting economic development, and managing the large influx of migrants. He said the United Nations would continue implementing its programs in coordination with the Islamic Emirate to better address the needs of the Afghan people. Governor Islam Jar highlighted the local administration's efforts to combat corruption and narcotics, advance major economic projects, and improve public services, reaffirming Herat's commitment to continued cooperation with the United Nations. #TOLOnews_English

Chaque fois une bonne raison : les ingérences étrangères, l'intérêt des enfants, les « valeurs européennes ». Signed into law the Sovereign Wealth Fund Bill, 2026, establishing a national investment vehicle aimed at preserving wealth generated from Kenya's natural resources and strategic investments for future generations. The new law is a historic milestone that will ensure the country's prosperity endures beyond the current generation. With this consequential law, Kenya has put in place watertight mechanisms that will ensure the resources attained from strategic assets and natural resources endure for generations. The Sovereign Wealth Fund serves as a guarantee that revenues from petroleum and other valuable mineral resources are not entirely consumed by the present generation but are invested to benefit our children and the children of our children. The legislation establishes three key windows under the fund: The Stabilisation Fund will cushion the economy against external shocks, the Strategic Investment Window will finance national development projects and create jobs, while the Future Generations pillar - Urithi Fund - will invest a portion of petroleum and mineral revenues for future citizens. Under the law, 30 per cent of revenues from petroleum and mineral resources will be channelled into the Urithi Fund, with the remainder supporting economic stability and strategic investments. The Sovereign Wealth Fund becomes the second major financial institution created under the Government's economic transformation agenda after the establishment of the National Infrastructure Fund in March 2026. This fund is designed to mobilise private capital for development projects.

اسلام آباد : 8 جولائی، 2026 وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیر صدارت گلگت بلتستان کے لئے 100 میگا واٹ شمسی توانائی منصوبے پر جائزہ اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ ماحول دوست صاف، سستی اور پائیدار توانائی کے فروغ کے لیے شمسی توانائی کا فروغ قومی توانائی کا اہم جزو ہے. 100 میگاواٹ سولر منصوبہ وفاقی حکومت کی جانب سے گلگت بلتستان کے عوام کے لیے ایک تحفہ ہے. پاور ڈویژن منصوبے کی تنصیب اور بروقت تکمیل کے حوالے سے اپنی ذمے داری پوری کرے. وزیرِ اعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ سولر منصوبے کیلئے خریداری کے عمل میں مکمل شفافیت یقینی بنائی جائے. تمام ادائیگیاں تیسرے فریق کی توثیق (Third-Party Validation) کے بعد کی جائیں. اجلاس کو گلگت بلتستان شمسی توانائی منصوبے پر پیشرفت کے حوالے سے بریفنگ بھی دی گئی. اجلاس کو بتایا گیا کہ منصوبے کے تحت 499 سرکاری عمارتوں کی چھتوں پر بیٹری اسٹوریج سمیت 18 میگاواٹ سولر سسٹم دسمبر 2026 تک نصب کر دیا جائے گا. 82 میگاواٹ یوٹیلٹی اسکیل سولر منصوبے کا پی سی ون منظوری کے لیے ایکنک (ECNEC) کو بھجوا دیا گیا.82 میگاواٹ سولر منصوبے سے تقریباً 13 لاکھ افراد مستفید ہوں گے. منصوبے کی تکمیل سے گلگت بلتستان میں سروس کا معیار بہتر ہو گا اور لوڈ شیڈنگ کے خاتمے میں مدد ملے گی. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر برائے پاور ڈویژن سردار اویس لغاری، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ و ریلوے بلال اظہر کیانی اور متعلقہ اعلیٰ سرکاری افسران نے شرکت کی۔ Video

दिल्ली में संपत्ति पंजीकरण व्यवस्था अब और अधिक पारदर्शी, जवाबदेह और नियमसम्मत होगी। मुख्यमंत्री श्रीमती रेखा गुप्ता के निर्देश पर जीपीए (General Power of Attorney) से जुड़े मामलों की जांच और निगरानी के लिए सख्त व्यवस्था लागू की गई है। ▸ रक्त संबंधियों के अलावा अन्य व्यक्तियों के पक्ष में होने वाले सभी जीपीए मामलों की अनिवार्य जांच होगी। ▸ ऐसे सभी मामलों को उचित स्टांप शुल्क निर्धारण के लिए कलेक्टर ऑफ स्टांप के पास भेजना अनिवार्य होगा। ▸ प्रत्येक जीपीए दस्तावेज की गहन जांच कर यह सुनिश्चित किया जाएगा कि बिक्री, कब्जा हस्तांतरण या मालिकाना हक से जुड़े प्रावधानों के अनुरूप उचित स्टांप शुल्क लागू हो। ▸ कलेक्टर ऑफ स्टांप को 30 दिनों के भीतर कारण सहित आदेश जारी करना होगा। उचित स्टांप शुल्क के भुगतान के बिना ऐसे दस्तावेजों का पंजीकरण नहीं किया जाएगा। ▸ एक महीने के भीतर ऑनलाइन ट्रैकिंग प्रणाली विकसित की जाएगी तथा सभी मामलों की नियमित निगरानी सुनिश्चित होगी। ▸ नियमों का उल्लंघन करने वाले अधिकारियों के विरुद्ध कड़ी अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की जाएगी। पारदर्शी प्रशासन, सुरक्षित राजस्व और नागरिकों के हितों की रक्षा के लिए दिल्ली सरकार पूरी प्रतिबद्धता के साथ कार्य कर रही है।

Climate change does not create gender inequality. It deepens it. In our latest EPWD blog, Anjhana Ramesh and Vandita Sahay highlight why the burden of a warming world falls unevenly on women. With women’s employment concentrated in climate-sensitive sectors such as agriculture, construction, and informal work, they face higher exposure to climate shocks and a lower capacity to recover from them. The burden extends into their homes as well. As water, fuel, and food grow scarcer, the unpaid work of securing them also intensifies. Schemes such as Ujjwala, Surya Ghar, and PM-KUSUM have begun to ease this load, but access alone is not the finish line. The argument is that women cannot remain only beneficiaries of climate policy. They must help shape it, from village councils to national decision-making, so that adaptation strategies reflect the realities of those carrying the heaviest costs. A more climate-resilient world and a more equal world are not separate goals. They are the same one. Read the full piece here: epwd-icrier.in/blog/macro-an…

Heat can make people seriously ill. Knowing the signs saves lives. ⚠️Here’s what to watch out for: Headache, dizziness, nausea, cramps, palpitations, excessive sweating or unusual tiredness. Heat and air pollution together hit harder and for people with cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, the effects can be faster and more severe. If you or someone you know starts to experience signs of heat stress: ❎ Slow down or stop activity, move to a cooling area, drink water. Seek help if your symptoms don’t improve. 🚨 Look for danger signs: severe headache, confusion, agitation, collapse, seizures, or not responding normally. This counts as a health emergency. 👀 If someone near you looks unwell, don’t leave them alone. Move them to a cooling area immediately, and call for first aid or alert event staff. 🌡️ Check weather forecast and air quality levels. Share to help more people recognize the signs.

Climate change does not create gender inequality. It deepens it. In our latest EPWD blog, Anjhana Ramesh and Vandita Sahay highlight why the burden of a warming world falls unevenly on women. With women’s employment concentrated in climate-sensitive sectors such as agriculture, construction, and informal work, they face higher exposure to climate shocks and a lower capacity to recover from them. The burden extends into their homes as well. As water, fuel, and food grow scarcer, the unpaid work of securing them also intensifies. Schemes such as Ujjwala, Surya Ghar, and PM-KUSUM have begun to ease this load, but access alone is not the finish line. The argument is that women cannot remain only beneficiaries of climate policy. They must help shape it, from village councils to national decision-making, so that adaptation strategies reflect the realities of those carrying the heaviest costs. A more climate-resilient world and a more equal world are not separate goals. They are the same one. Read the full piece here: epwd-icrier.in/blog/macro-an…

The 2nd Regional Forum on the ASCC Strategic Plan concluded on 3 July 2026, marking the successfulcompletion of the three-day forum. During the panel discussion, the Secretary-General of AIPA; the Deputy Director of the Environmental and Natural Resources Division, Ministry of Economy, Malaysia; the Undersecretary of the Department of Economy, Planning and Development of the Philippines and Chair of the Subcommittee on SDGs; and the Executive Directors of the ASEAN Centre for Biodiversity and the ASEAN Centre for Sustainable Development Studies and Dialogue shared best practices on mainstreaming regional plans into legislation, national development plans, and sustainable development cooperation. The panellists underscored the need for systematic mapping of the ASCC Strategic Plan’s Strategic Goals, Objectives, and Strategic Measures into national and sectoral plans and frameworks and underlined the importance of strong commitments from relevant actors to ensure the successful implementation of the Strategic Plan. The final day of the forum also featured group discussions in which participants discussed the foundations, strategies, and recommendations for the mainstreaming of the ASCC Strategic Plan. In-person and online participants identified mainstreaming entry points, enabling mechanisms, and key practical recommendations, which will guide ASEAN Member States and relevant stakeholders in their efforts to mainstream the ASCC Strategic Plan. The three-day Regional Forum was attended by more than 300 participants from ASEAN Member States; ASEAN Dialogue Partners, Development Partners, and Sectoral Dialogue Partners; ASEAN Centres and Entities; Civil Society Organisations; and academia and think tanks. The 2nd Regional Forum is part of the “Supporting the Development of the ASCC Strategic Plan” project, funded by the Government of Japan through the Japan-ASEAN Integration Fund (JAIF) 3.0. #ASEAN #ASEANCommunity #ASCCStrategicPlan #ASCCPost2025 #JapanASEANIntegrationFund #JAIF #ACV2045 #ASEANJapan

In 3 months, India hosted Japan PM with 16 agreements on defense and AI, South Korea President with a $50 billion trade target, and is now sending Modi to Indonesia, Australia, and New Zealand Japan brings manufacturing and defense tech, South Korea brings semiconductors and shipbuilding. Australia brings critical minerals. Indonesia controls the strait between two oceans. This is not random summit travel, India is quietly building a working network of Asia strongest industrial and maritime economies, separate from both Washington and Beijing India trades $150 billion a year with China, Cutting that is not an option. The point is to reduce the parts of that dependence that can be used against you. That is why India signed a critical minerals agreement with the US and Japan worth $20 billion in May. Why Australia holds 21 of the 49 minerals India needs for batteries and chips. Why India and Japan launched their first joint defense production project this month. Nobody is decoupling. Everybody is building a second source. Japan, South Korea, Australia, and Indonesia all have choices. They deepen ties with India only if India makes itself worth deepening ties with. Right now, defense manufacturing is growing but not fast enough. Procurement cycles are still slow. Factory approvals still take too long. Summit agreements look good on paper. Converting them into running production lines takes years of reform at home. The gap between India diplomatic ambition and its industrial readiness is where this whole idea will be tested, lets see what lie in the future But this is strong Signal and Yu cannot avoid this :)

That’s precisely why India needs a sovereign aero-engine ecosystem. The data points to an industry-wide bottleneck—not an India-only story. Nearly 27 million Americans, or 8% of the U.S. population, live in areas where water demand consistently approaches or exceeds naturally available water supply. Until recently, accessing comprehensive water availability information with national coverage required stitching together disparate datasets across multiple agencies, regions, and complicated websites. The Data Companion eliminates these barriers by: 💧 Providing consistent information about water availability and use across approximately 80,000 watersheds nationwide from 2000 to 2020 💧 Enabling data access through various user-friendly means, including a subset and download tool, a data file directory, an API, and a new interactive map 💧 Continually adding new and updated data to reflect the latest USGS water models and science Check out the interactive map now: water.usgs.gov/nwaa-data/ 📷 1: View of soil moisture data for January 2020 across the lower 48 United States from the Data Companion web mapper.

Political scientist Ian Bremmer thinks the biggest geopolitical shift in the Middle East isn't happening in Iran, it's happening in Washington. For decades, America's support for Israel wasn't up for debate; it was one of the few issues Republicans and Democrats broadly agreed on. Ian thinks that era is ending. He pointed to Rahm Emanuel, one of the Democratic establishment's most influential voices, publicly describing Israel as a "territorial pariah." Those are the words not from a progressive firebrand, or a fringe activist, but from a centrist who has spent years firmly in Israel's corner. Then Ian pointed to JD Vance becoming increasingly critical of Israel, Tucker Carlson openly attacking Israeli policy, and even Trump publicly praising Erdogan while becoming noticeably colder toward Netanyahu. Americans instinctively root for the underdog, and for years, they saw Israel as one. Today, he says more and more Americans see it as a wealthy, technologically dominant, nuclear-armed regional power. That's a profound psychological shift because once voters stop seeing an ally as the weaker side, they begin judging its actions by a completely different standard. The biggest threat to Israel's long-term position may be the slow collapse of the political consensus that has protected it in Washington for decades. And if that consensus really is breaking apart, it will reshape American foreign policy across the entire Middle East. @ianbremmer Video

President Donald Trump has joined fellow leaders at the NATO summit in Turkey, which runs from July 7-8, at a time when the future of the alliance—and U.S. commitments to Europe—are being debated. "When debating U.S. grand strategy, foreign policy elites often frame alliances as either a legacy asset or a growing liability," writes expert @m2matthijs. "The question today is not whether alliances matter. It is how they should adapt to a world in which American power is eroding, geopolitical competition is intensifying, and U.S. allies are growing more autonomous." "But the nature of those alliances will have to change if they are to endure,” writes Matthijs. “They will have to become more reciprocal, more selective, and more grounded in capabilities, because the old model of asymmetric dependence is no longer politically sustainable," he argues. "The challenge is most acute for the transatlantic alliance," writes Matthijs. "For decades, the United States and Europe operated under a clear bargain. Washington provided security and its European allies gave their loyalty. But it depended on assumptions—about U.S. reliability, shared threat perceptions, and a broadly liberal international order—that no longer hold." "A looser, more transactional, but also potentially more resilient system is emerging. The United States will remain the anchor of European security, but Europeans will do far more for themselves," he writes. “The adjustment will be tough. A more autonomous Europe will resist American pressure, chart its own course on economic and regulatory issues, and seek greater control over its own security and industrial policies. But the alternative . . . would be far more damaging to U.S. global interests.” "The United States' interests will undoubtedly be better served with strong and capable partners—rather than weak and dependent ones."

India is the world's largest producer and exporter of rice, yet the Food Corporation of India (FCI) is holding rice stocks that are nearly five times the prescribed buffer norm, at a carrying cost of over Rs. 10,712 crores in FY25. In their latest article, Ashok Gulati, Ritika Juneja, and Purvi Thangaraj trace this surplus to three interlinked policy distortions: open-ended MSP procurement, with several states offering bonuses above the MSP; free electricity and heavily subsidised urea. Instead of addressing these underlying distortions, the government's response has been to divert surplus rice to ethanol production, supplying rice to distilleries at Rs. 23/kg despite FCI's economic cost of about Rs. 44/kg on the justification that it is broken and damaged rice. The authors also highlight the environmental costs of the current policy framework, including the use of ~ 4,000 litres of water to produce one kilogram of rice, high methane emissions from paddy cultivation, and nitrate contamination of groundwater associated with serious health risks. To address these challenges, the authors recommend capping state procurement at 40% of production, discontinuing state MSP bonuses, limiting free PDS supplies to the most vulnerable households, shifting ethanol production towards maize, and replacing fertiliser subsidies with direct income support. Masked individuals holding Confederate flags and upside-down Stars and Stripes were seen marching through the streets of Washington D.C. during celebrations of the United States’ 250th birthday on Saturday, July 4. Footage by Olivia Rondeau shows the group marching outside her window, banging drums and carrying shields, while wearing a uniform of white masks, blue shirts, and khaki pants. The group wore identical attire to Patriot Front, a white supremacist group, who previously gained attention for organizing a similar demonstration in Nashville, Tennessee on July 7, 2024. Storyful cannot confirm whether the individuals marching in D.C. were Patriot Front members. “What they stand for is nothing I could possibly agree with, but one of the foundational principles of the United States which makes democracy messy is free speech,” Interior Secretary Doug Ingram told CNN when asked about condemning the group’s protests. It is also one of the strongest safeguards against poverty, exclusion and extremism. The international community must not look away. Humanitarian aid remains indispensable, but it is not enough. STATEMENT OF THE CONFERENCE OF HEADS OF THE CARIBBEAN COMMUNITY (CARICOM) ON THE REAPPOINTMENT OF THE SECRETARY GENERAL During the Retreat of Heads of Government of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) held on 06 July 2026, the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago maintained its objection to the process used in the reappointment of the Secretary General of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM). CARICOM acknowledged that the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago desires to have the issue of the reappointment of the SG referred to the Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ) to render an Advisory Opinion thereon. To facilitate this request, the Community agrees to commence proceedings to secure such advisory opinion in accordance with Article 212 of the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas. The Community acknowledged that this is the very purpose for which the CCJ was created – to be a treaty interpretation body. The Community further agreed that the status quo with respect to the re-appointment of the Secretary General shall remain unless and until the Community considers the said Advisory Opinion from the CCJ. The Community agreed that this way forward allows for this matter to be resolved in an amicable manner, without prejudice to the ability of the Community to conduct its affairs. In this context, the Community reaffirmed that the ongoing review of its governance architecture is part of the broader mandate, agreed at the previous Conference in St. Kitts and Nevis, to strengthen the governance of the Community and enhance its effectiveness. The Heads of Government further underscored that this process does not impugn the integrity of any Member State or individual; rather it reflects the Community’s collective commitment to continuous institutional improvement with the highest standards of good governance. The Heads of Government have reaffirmed their commitment to the ideals and objectives of the Community and will continue to move forward in unity to advance the interests of the Region during these difficult times, recognizing the myriad of challenges the Community faces currently.

National water availability data at your fingertips! 💧🎉 The National Water Availability Assessment Data Companion provides regularly updated, model-based estimates of water availability and use on a national scale. Nearly 27 million Americans, or 8% of the U.S. population, live in areas where water demand consistently approaches or exceeds naturally available water supply. Until recently, accessing comprehensive water availability information with national coverage required stitching together disparate datasets across multiple agencies, regions, and complicated websites. The Data Companion eliminates these barriers by: 💧 Providing consistent information about water availability and use across approximately 80,000 watersheds nationwide from 2000 to 2020 💧 Enabling data access through various user-friendly means, including a subset and download tool, a data file directory, an API, and a new interactive map 💧 Continually adding new and updated data to reflect the latest USGS water models and science Check out the interactive map now: water.usgs.gov/nwaa-data/ 📷 1: View of soil moisture data for January 2020 across the lower 48 United States from the Data Companion web mapper.

Let's unpack the state of USMCA renegotiations following the announcement last week that the US "did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form." 1. As has been widely noted, the US announcement was expected and is not the demise of the USMCA. Rather, USMCA countries are continuing to negotiate while the agreement ticks towards an expiration in 2036. Odds are high that the US, Mexico, and Canada will reach a deal much, much sooner than 2036.... 2. I bet the US and Mexico reach a preliminary renewal deal sometime this year, though perhaps not before the midterms. Mexico has been willing to address a number of US concerns (e.g., it has increased tariffs on its imports of Chinese products) and Trump has a reasonably warm relationship with Sheinbaum, which bodes well for negotiations. I could see the US closing a new deal with Mexico first and then trying to jam the Canadians, given more complicated US-Canada political dynamics. (This also happened in 2018 when the US and Mexico reached a deal more than a month before Canada closed). 3. Substantively, the issue I am most interested in is revisions to rules of origin (ROOs). Specifically, the US is reportedly pushing for North American content requirements in a number of different kinds of manufactured products, not just the autos and textiles covered by the USMCA. Developing regional content rules for products such as machinery and electronics, however, is technically complicated and I will be interested to see what USTR can land. I will also be interested in whether the US succeeds in its bid to establish *US* content rules for some products, and not just *North American* content rules. ROOs matter not just for USMCA trade but because USTR will likely, longer-term, try to incorporate the type of ROOs developed for USMCA into other trade agreements. 4. I am also watching the overall effective tariff rate for Mexico and Canada and the rate for specific products. I expect Mexico and Canada will continue to have preferential tariff rates relative to most of the world, because I expect many USMCA products will continue to enter the US tariff free. But the 232 tariffs add a wrinkle here, especially for autos--if the US tries to set too high a rate on North American auto parts (or, as Jason Miller has pointed, tries to set too high a US content requirement), the US risks inadvertently disadvantaging North American cars compared to European, Japanese, and Korean cars, which face a tariff rate capped at 15% under Trump trade deals. 5. Finally, I will be fascinated to see the legal structure the Trump Administration tries to use to implement its changes to the USMCA. I would be surprised if the Trump Administration wants to go back to Congress for implementation, given congressional political dynamics. Instead, my bet is that USTR essentially tries to layer a complex set of Section 301 (and 232) tariffs on top of the existing USMCA to implement "USMCA revisions." But we will see.

In many low and middle-income countries, healthcare professionals face immense barriers such as unreliable internet, a lack of localized content, and language gaps that can delay critical care. To bridge this gap, Techies Without Borders built an AI-powered experimental platform that acts as a localized "doctor's assistant." Frontline workers can now type in a medical query and receive an instant, evidence-based answer in their own language. Thanks to NVIDIA AI and accelerated computing, medical insights that used to take 5 agonizing minutes to load are now delivered in just 2 seconds. And because it runs locally on edge devices, a lack of internet connection is no longer a barrier to saving lives. This isn't just a technical achievement; it's a lifeline for clinics facing severe physician shortages.

Pakistan and Bulgaria held the sixth round of Bilateral Political Consultations in Islamabad. The Pakistan delegation was led by Ambassador Ayesha Ali, Additional Secretary (Europe) while the Bulgarian side was headed by H.E. Ambassador Petko Doykov, Director General for Bilateral Relations, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Bulgaria. The two sides reviewed the full range of bilateral relations and discussed ways to expand political engagement and cooperation in trade, investment, defence, parliamentary exchanges, culture, education, ICT and people-to-people contacts. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments and cooperation at multilateral forums. Both sides agreed to hold the next round of Consultations in Sofia, Bulgaria at mutually agreed dates. The Head of Bulgarian delegation Ambassador Doykov also called on the Foreign Secretary Ambassador Amna Baloch @amnabaloch4 . The Foreign Secretary shared Pakistan’s perspective on key regional developments, including Pakistan’s mediation role in the US-Iran conflict.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a meeting to review Pakistan’s ongoing engagement with various multilateral initiatives. The DPM/FM was briefed on the status of preparations for various upcoming high-level events. He underscored Pakistan’s continued commitment to strengthening multilateralism and gave necessary directions regarding Pakistan’s normative positions at various forums. The meeting was attended by the Foreign Secretary Ambassador Amna Baloch, Special Secretary (UN), Additional Secretary (Asia Pacific), and other senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ہوئے جس کے سبب اسی عطار کے لونڈے سے دوا لیتے ہیں حالانکہ میر تقی میر کے کوئی بھی مستند کلیات کا مطالعہ کر لیں تو آپ کو معلوم ہو جائے گا کہ میر نے شعر کے دوسرے مصرع میں لونڈے کا لفظ ہرگز استعمال نہیں عقاب کی وجہ سے یہ شعر علامہ اقبال سے منسوب کر دیا جاتا ہے اور سید صادق حسین ایڈووکیٹ کو ان کے اکلوتے مشہورِ زمانہ شعر سے بھی محروم کر دیا جاتا ہے۔ اردو کا ایک ضرب المثل شعر مقررین اکثر اپنی تقاریر اور کالم نویس اپنے کالموں میں استعمال کرتے ہیں .... وہ آئے بزم میں اتنا تو میر نے دیکھا پھر اُس کے بعد چراغوں میں روشنی نہ رہی یہ شعر آغا شاعر قزلباش کے ایک شاگرد مہاراج بہادر برق کا ہے اور غلط طور پر میر تقی میر سے منسوب ہے۔ آپ میر کے چھ دیوان پڑھ لیں کہیں بھی آپ کو یہ شعر نظر نہیں آئے گا۔ دہلی میں 1884ءمیں پیدا ہونے والے مہاراج بہادر برق کے مذکورہ بالا شعر کا پہلا مصرع اچھی یاد کر لیں ع وہ آئے بزم میں اتنا تو برق نے دیکھا بہادر شاہ ظفر کا درج ذیل کس نے نہیں سُنا ہو گا کتنا ہے بدنصیب ظفر، دفن کے لئے دو گز زمین بھی نہ ملی کوئے یار میں عوام الناس نے اسی غزل کے حوالے سے ایک اور شعر بھی بہادر شاہ ظفر سے منسوب کر رکھا ہے عمر دراز مانگ کے لائے تھے چار دن دو آرزو میں کٹ گئے، دو انتظار میں یہ شعر بہادر شاہ ظفر کا بالکل نہیں بلکہ سیماب اکبر آبادی کا ہے۔ ان کی 1947ءمیں شائع ہونے والی کتاب ”کلیم عجم“ میرے پاس بھی موجود ہے۔ جس شخص کو شبہ ہو اسے سیماب اکبر آبادی کی پوری غزل کی فوٹو کاپی مہیا کی جا سکتی ہے۔ سیماب نے زیر بحث شعر کا پہلا مصرع اس طرح کہا تھا ع عمر دراز، مانگ کے لائی تھی چار دن بڑے پڑھے لکھے اور اعلیٰ ادبی ذوق رکھنے والے حضرات بھی درج ذیل شعر کو کبھی علامہ اقبال اور کبھی حالی سے منسوب کر دیتے ہیں خدا نے آج تک اس قوم کی حالت نہیں بدلی نہ ہو جس کو خیال آپ اپنی حالت کے بدلنے کا یہ شعر قرآن حکیم کی آیت کا ترجمہ ہے اور یہ منظوم تخلیقی ترجمہ مولانا ظفر علی خان نے کیا ہے۔ یہ شعر 1937ءمیں شائع ہونے والی مولانا ظفر علی خان کی کتاب ”بہارستان“ میں شامل ہے۔ ایک اور شعر جو کبھی میر تقی میر اور کبھی امیر مینائی سے منسوب کر دیا جاتا ہے وہ یہ ہے شکست و فتح نصیبوں سے ہے ولے اے میر مقابلہ تو دلِ ناتواں نے خوب کیا یہ شعر نہ تو میر تقی میر کا ہے اور نہ ہی امیر مینائی کا ہے بلکہ یہ شعر محمد یار خاں امیر کا ہے اور شعر کا درست متن بھی یوں ہے شکست و فتح میاں اتفاق ہے لیکن مقابلہ تو دلِ ناتواں نے خوب کیا مصحفی کا یہ شعر ضرب المثل کی طرح مشہور ہے مَیں عجب یہ رسم دیکھی، مجھے روزِ عیدِ قرباں وہی ذبح بھی کرے ہے، وہی لے ثواب اُلٹا یہی شعر پہلے مصرعے کی تبدیلی کے ساتھ اِنشا سے بھی منسوب ہے یہ عجیب ماجرا ہے کہ بروزِ عیدِ قرباں وہی ذبح بھی کرے ہے وہی لے ثواب الُٹا قاضی عبدالودود نے تحقیق کے بعد نے لچک دی ہے اُتنا ہی یہ اُبھرے گا جتنا کہ دبا دیں گے (صفی لکھنوی) اس کو ناقدری عالم کا صلہ کہتے ہیں مر چکے ہم تو زمانے نے بہت یاد کیا (برج نرائن چکبست) افسوس بے شمار سخن ہائے گفتنی خوف فساد خلق سے By targeting a Saudi and a Qatari tanker in the Strait of Hormuz #Iran is trying to send a signal that neither the signing of the MoU with the U.S. nor its desire to improve relations with the Gulf Arab states should be interpreted as a green light for regional countries to move freely through the strait while disregarding Tehran's claim to control and manage the waterway. In that sense, it reflects the view that geopolitical considerations outweigh the diplomatic constraints that, in the past, gave rise to the policy of so-called "strategic patience" as the overarching approach of the Islamic Republic. This shift, of course, began during the war itself, when Iran targeted not only U.S. bases but also locations in Arab countries around the Persian Gulf. The message is that this approach continues. In the same vein, from Tehran's perspective, long-term strategic value of the Strait of Hormuz outweighs the potential economic benefits of an agreement with the United States or improved relations with the Gulf countries. This should also be viewed in the context of other recent developments, such as Iran's attempt to break the air blockade of #Yemen by sending a passenger aircraft. It reflects Iran's perception that it currently enjoys a stronger regional position, with its status having been elevated, and that the Gulf countries should accommodate Iran's priorities and take its strategic considerations into account. At the same time, however, this approach carries considerable risks, including the possibility of alienating the Arab countries and, if handled poorly, even Iran's own partners, such as Russia and China. Both showed considerable sympathy toward Iran during the war, particularly China, but that could change. For this reason, some analysts and experts in Iran argue that, alongside the negotiations with the United States and Iran's ongoing activities in the Strait of Hormuz and elsewhere in the region, Tehran should establish a high-ranking, permanent, and institutionalized channel of communication and coordination with China and Russia in order to keep them on board.

⚠️ #IFCIOR | PIRACY UPDATE 02 – WESTERN IOR | AS ON 1300 UTC 07 JUL 26 Piracy-related activity in the Western Indian Ocean continues to indicate a sustained and adaptive threat pattern. Since 26 May 26, IFC-IOR has recorded 14 piracy-related incidents, comprising 06 attacks and 08 suspicious approaches / attempts, with 02 incidents actioned by Indian Navy. 📌 Assessment of the chronology and spatial distribution of incidents indicates that 02 Pirate Action Groups (PAGs) are likely active, one along the Al Mukalla–Bosaso axis and another operating off Aden. The distribution of incidents suggests that piracy-linked activity is not isolated, but reflects a wider operating pattern across the Gulf of Aden and adjoining approaches. 🌊 Recent incidents also indicate a shift of piracy-linked activity from Somali basin towards the Gulf of Aden. This is likely influenced by prevailing rough sea conditions in the wider Western IOR, which may be pushing skiffs towards relatively sheltered waters and more predictable merchant traffic routes. 🚢 The incident profile shows a clear focus on larger merchant vessels, including tankers, bulk carriers and cargo/container ships. This indicates that PAG activity remains oriented towards high-value commercial shipping rather than small local craft. 🛡️ Indian Navy actions involving MV MASHALLAH 1, MV FAREEDA 5 and MV GOLDEN ARSENAL highlight the operational value of early reporting, rapid IFC-IOR information fusion and coordinated maritime security response. These actions helped compress the response timeline and enabled timely intervention before incidents could escalate further. 📢 Masters, CSOs and operators transiting the affected area are advised to maintain heightened vigilance, implement BMP (MS) measures, keep citadel and emergency response procedures ready, maintain continuous watch, and report all suspicious activity without delay to IFC-IOR and maritime reporting centres. 📧 Report incidents / suspicious activity: ifc-ior.gurugram@navy.gov.in @indiannavy #MaritimeSecurity

I convened an emergency WHO/Europe check-in on extreme heat with one direct question: what has this heatwave taught us, and are we ready for what comes next? The call brought together 130+ participants from 41 Member States, as well as the European Commission and civil society. The key takeaway was clear: heat-health action plans work. Even as excess deaths are reported, many more lives are protected when plans are in place, tested and linked to public health response. We heard concrete examples from Italy, France, Spain and others: surveillance providing near real-time data; coordination across sectors reducing pressure on health services; and close work with media improving public risk communication. But gaps remain: fewer than half of Member States have national heat-health action plans; cooling spaces are not always available or known; and older people living alone, long-term care residents and homeless people are still not reached consistently. @WHO_Europe will share lessons, support countries directly and continue these rapid check-ins, as Member States requested. The NATO summit in Turkey, which kicks off on July 7, could be the start of a transition toward a new version of the alliance where Europe needs to accelerate their own defense planning with less U.S. assistance, expert @LianaFix argues. “For the United States, a Europe capable of defending itself against Russia but unable to project power beyond its borders is a mixed blessing,” Fix writes. “Ultimately, a Europe that is strong—militarily, economically, and technologically—serves U.S. interests, even if it increasingly acts in its own.” The United States appears to be pulling back from European security, with U.S. plans for withdrawal accelerating after a rift over support for the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran, Fix argues. There are fears the move could leave European security worse off, she notes. An energy crisis, widening innovation gap, falling productivity growth, and limited bandwidth to deal with other regions mean that Europe, at least for the next decade, will struggle to project power globally, Fix writes. Europe “should be able to deter Russian aggression on its own, but it will lose geoeconomic ground, especially to China,” she writes. “A Europe that defends itself at home but loses influence abroad seems the likeliest outcome.”

Rural development is one of the most powerful investments we can make in global prosperity, food security and stability. Small farms of up to five hectares produce around half of the world’s food. Behind this are rural women, men and young people working at the first mile of food systems — growing food, powering local economies and building resilient communities. On World Rural Development Day, we recognize their essential role. At @IFAD, we invest in the first mile of food systems — where rural people, their skills and their enterprises drive lasting change for their communities. These investments increase production, improve access to markets, strengthen value chains and build resilience to shocks. When rural communities have access to finance, technology and opportunity, incomes grow, food security improves and societies become more stable and resilient. #WorldRuralDevelopmentDay | #FinancingTheFirstMile Video
